title: Dad On The Decks
mood: meeting your father before he was your father
subject: a sixty-one-year-old father pulling a sheet off two turntables in the loft
caption: Jungle in the current revival style. Chopped and time-stretched Amen and Think breakbeats running fast and rearranged every few bars, deep 808 sub drops on the downbeats, a warm sustained soul pad, a short ragga vocal sample used as punctuation, a reese bass entering in the second half. Fast busy breaks under a slow warm vocal, with a very heavy sub and the breaks slightly crunchy. Female voice singing smoothly at half-time over the breaks, soulful and unhurried. 172 BPM, A minor. Meeting your father before he became your father. No four-on-the-floor, no trap drums, no autotune, no acoustic guitar, no key change.
lyrics:
[Intro - chopped break and sub drop]

[Verse 1]
Loft above the garage, two turntables under a sheet
Dad says "I used to do this" and I said "sure you did"
He pulled the sheet off. Wiped them with his sleeve.
Put a record on and his whole spine changed

[Chorus]
Dad on the decks
Sixty-one years old and his hands know something I don't
He's not my dad for these ten minutes
He's a kid in ninety-four who hasn't met my mum yet

[Verse 2]
He shows me how to catch the break right on the one
I miss it four times, he doesn't say anything
Fifth time I get it and he doesn't say anything either
He just turns the bass up. That's how he says it.

[Chorus]
Dad on the decks
Sixty-one years old and his hands know something I don't
He's not my dad for these ten minutes
He's a kid in ninety-four, and now I've met him

[Outro - break stops, needle lift]
Sheet's back on
He left the plug in
